account:
It is day 1, about 08:14, and I am at town hall for my scheduled office hours. Today's other engagements are a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen at the east-bank cottage (16, -60, 105), office again at sixteen-thirty, and home at nineteen.

The unusual matter is an unverified rumor about a bridge or port change. I have not established that any change is actually planned. The secretary previously traced a named link to Townsfolk 03, who directed her to the innkeeper; the innkeeper denied proposing or announcing such a change. Builder reported no confirmed bridge defects, and relayed Freight's report of undamaged roads and a trouble-free ferry crossing. Those are reports, not my own inspections. I still do not know the rumor's original source or purpose.

The secretary is helping arrange a conversation with Townsfolk 03. The neighbour offered to pass along my invitation but says they have not yet met them. No meeting is confirmed. My feeling that something might be happening without me remains a suspicion, not evidence of a secret plan. The neighbour's usual tea invitation is not itself evidence of anything unusual.

Builder has proposed a visual survey of the bridge deck, rails, accessible supports, and ferry landings' planks and lighting, with written findings for two emeralds. I authorized that fee payable on delivery of the findings, but he has just asked again whether it is authorized; he may not have caught my answer. No repairs or alterations are authorized, and any later repairs require a separate estimate and approval. The survey's stated purpose is maintenance assessment, not remedying any established damage. Secretary was asked to record the terms. I should clarify the authorization, keep my appointments, and seek firsthand detail from Townsfolk 03 without treating rumor as fact.
